name: Graphic Arts
tagline: Got an idea? Let’s turn it into something people can see, share, and remember!
description:
In Graphic Arts, students learn how to think like designers and create like professionals. From bold logos and eye-catching advertisements to magazine layouts, T-shirts, packaging, and digital graphics, students use Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign to bring their ideas to life.

Along the way, students explore color, composition, typography, branding, and visual communication while building a portfolio of real-world design projects. Whether you’re already a creative pro or just discovering your design skills, there’s always something new to create!

courses.title: Intro to Graphic Design
courses.desc:
Students explore the fundamentals of graphic design through hands-on projects that introduce color, typography, composition, branding, layout, and visual communication.

Using industry-standard Adobe software, students learn the basics of Illustrator, and Photoshop while creating everything from logos and advertisements to digital graphics and print projects.

No previous design experience is needed — just curiosity, creativity, and a willingness to try new things! This course gives students the foundation they need to continue through the Graphic Design and Graphic Communication pathways while discovering how creative ideas can become real-world designs.

courses.title: Graphics Design and Production
courses.desc:
In Graphic Design & Production, students build on the skills they learned in Intro and begin working more like professional graphic designers. Students tackle larger, more challenging projects while developing their skills in Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign.

From creating logos and brand identities to posters, publications, packaging, T-shirts, and other print and digital projects, students learn how to take a design from an initial idea all the way to a finished product.

Students also get hands-on experience with print production and the graphic arts process, learning how designs are prepared, produced, and turned into something you can actually hold, wear, and share.

More creativity. More projects. More real-world design experience. This is where students start building a portfolio that shows what they can really do!

courses.title: Advanced Graphic Design
courses.desc:
You’ve learned the tools. Now it’s time to make them your own!

Advanced Graphic Design is the capstone of the Graphic Design pathway and challenges students to push their creativity, sharpen their design skills, and begin working more like professional designers. Students take on complex, real-world design projects that require thoughtful concepts, strong visual communication, and attention to detail.

Using Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign, students explore advanced techniques in branding, typography, illustration, advertising, publication design, packaging, and digital media. Projects are designed to give students creative freedom while teaching them how to develop an idea, respond to a design challenge, and produce polished, professional-quality work.

Students also begin developing their personal design style and professional portfolio, preparing them for future careers, internships, college programs, and creative opportunities.

Bigger ideas. Stronger skills. More creative freedom. This is where students stop simply learning graphic design and start discovering what kind of designer they want to be.

courses.title: Advanced Graphic Outputs and Processes
courses.desc:
Ready to take the lead? Your designs are only part of the job—now you’re running the show!

Advanced Graphic Output Processes is the capstone of the Graphic Communication pathway, where students take on the role of designer, project manager, and team leader. Students work on larger, more complex projects that require them to plan, organize, communicate, problem-solve, and meet real-world deadlines.

Students learn what it takes to move a project from concept to completion while working with clients, collaborating with team members, delegating responsibilities, managing production schedules, and making sure the final product meets professional expectations.

Whether they’re developing branding, preparing files for print, producing apparel, creating promotional materials, or managing a team project, students gain experience with the behind-the-scenes skills that make a creative team successful.

Create it. Plan it. Produce it. Lead it. This is where students put everything they’ve learned to work and prepare for the next step into college, careers, and the creative industry.
